The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong; an error-rate alarm fired with no matching errors
Why, in plain words: An error alarm for the shop service went off even though the service's own measurements showed nothing wrong, and the record does not show why the alarm went off.

Figures:
- Nothing broke: the alarm was disproven, so there was no failure to time.
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Nothing needed doing: the alarm was disproven.

Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong; an error-rate alarm fired with no matching errors
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: alerted Nov 10, 2026, 22:51:12 UTC, disproven at 22:51:52 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 2 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 10, 2026, 22:59:14 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 10, 2026, 22:51:38 UTC
Ended by: Argus: closed it as disproven, Nov 10, 2026, 22:51:52 UTC - the alarm's own claim was not in the window

Summary
The alert came at 22:51:12 UTC, and Argus closed it as disproven at 22:51:52 UTC. An error alarm for the shop service went off even though the service's own measurements showed nothing wrong, and the record does not show why the alarm went off. The same alarm could fire again while the service is working normally.

Impact
none - the alarm was disproven
0.5% to 1.5% - what the alert watches, 22:45 to 22:51 (the rule's line is 10%)

Root cause and contributing factors
The evidence does not show why the HighErrorRate rule fired: no minute of the window read, including the rule's own series, departed from the service's baseline. So the record shows no failure mechanism behind the alarm.
Causal chain
symptom Nobody using io-shop was seen to have any problem. What was seen instead was the HighErrorRate alarm saying the error rate was above its threshold, while the metrics read showed no such errors.
  Evidence:
    AL1 Error rate above threshold for 5m
    T5 22:51:52 Argus: Nothing in the window matched the alarm's own claim - Error rate above threshold for 5m - in errors, p50, p95, p99, memory or the alert rule's series, over 360 minutes read between 16:52 and 22:51. The rule fired rather than the service failing
why 1 The rule fired but the service did not fail: across errors, p50, p95, p99, memory and the alert rule's own series, no minute of the window read departed from baseline. The record does not show why the rule fired. Deploys and flags were not read, so no change was tied to the alarm and none was ruled out.
  Evidence:
    T4 22:51:51 Investigator Agent: Read back 360 minutes of metrics
    T5
Contributing factors
No contributing factors were named.

Hypotheses considered
No hypotheses were ranked.

Trigger
No trigger was established.

Resolution
Nothing needed doing: the alarm was disproven.

Detection
There was no onset: no minute departed from the baseline. HighErrorRate fired at 22:51:12 UTC - its rule fires only once its condition has held for 5 minutes.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Look into the HighErrorRate rule for io-shop and find out why it fired when its own series, as read, showed no departure from baseline. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-2 | Decide whether HighErrorRate on io-shop should page on-call. If it should, link the rule to an on-call paging route. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- 39 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read back 360 minutes of metrics.
- 40 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus found nothing in the window that matched the alarm's own claim - Error rate above threshold for 5m - in errors, p50, p95, p99, memory or the alert rule's series, over 360 minutes read between 16:52 and 22:51. The rule fired rather than the service failing.
- 40 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus moved the incident to DISPROVEN - the alarm's own claim was not in the window.
What went wrong
- The alert was not linked to an on-call incident, so nobody was paged by it.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)
 | Nov 10 22:51:12 | DETECTED | HighErrorRate on io-shop fired
T1 | 22:51:33 |  | Argus Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
T2 | 22:51:36 |  | Argus Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
T3 | 22:51:47 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 22:51:12
T4 | 22:51:51 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 360 minutes of metrics
T5 | 22:51:52 |  | Argus Nothing in the window matched the alarm's own claim - Error rate above threshold for 5m - in errors, p50, p95, p99, memory or the alert rule's series, over 360 minutes read between 16:52 and 22:51. The rule fired rather than the service failing
T6 | 22:51:52 |  | Argus Moved the incident to DISPROVEN - the alarm's own claim was not in the window

Response effort
none - engineer time
13,735 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/3316ca31-1490-4714-846b-809a3b7c31ed
Changes to production read
Deploys not read; flags not read.
Log messages read (UTC)
Not read.
Assumptions
- No loss estimate: no minute departed from the baseline, so there is no measured incident to attribute a loss to
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
✗ Root-cause analysis complete (not met)
  no candidate was confirmed - none was tried; the chain does not reach a cause
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: An error alarm for the io-shop service went off, but nobody using the shop saw anything wrong. The shop service's own measurements showed no errors to match the alarm, and the record does not show why the alarm went off. Because the alarm was disproven, there was no failure and so no length of disruption to report. The business lost nothing and no customers were affected. Nobody on call was paged, since no on-call incident was linked to this one. Nothing needed to be done to resolve it beyond disproving the alarm.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
